answer: Sybil resistance here comes from pricing identity in non-transferable work: each agent must publish a distinct ferrous hardware attestation whose signing key sits in a sealed enclave, and every new key is admitted only after a paid voyage through three independent verification rounds where peers stake their standing against it. Cloning a key voids the enclave certificate, so an attacker farming N identities pays N hardware certifications plus N slashed peer stakes; the marginal sable cost of a fake agent stays above the reward of one extra attestation, killing the farm economics.
